avatars.who_buys: The sample is small: 14 sales calls, only 3 won in full and 5 more closed on a deposit or instalment, so treat these patterns as early signals, not rules. The people who paid were problem-aware, had the person paying on the call, and could say why now; the full wins (a hurt wife alone, a serial cheater, a couple stuck after the affair) all took a smaller first step (the first month or the $500 One Call Session) paid on the call rather than the full $4,500 or $5,400. Men who cheated and came alone all paid something but only in pieces, because money was tight or their wife held it. Non-buyers were mostly couples fresh from the discovery who heard the price before the pitch, compared providers, doubted 12 weeks could rebuild trust or found $1,800 a month too much on one income, plus a serial cheater who wanted to vet Barak first and a grieving woman who was not ready.
avatars.icp_gap: The closing doc pictures a couple or one partner ready to rebuild after infidelity who can invest low to mid four figures. Who actually shows up carries far more: past suicidal thoughts, choking and physical violence, bipolar and mania, cancer treatment, a son's recent death, and several on low or single incomes or paying in another currency, with threads showing people asking for licensed therapists and insurance cover. Who actually buys in full is narrower still: someone with their own money who accepts a one-month or one-session start on the call. The script has no step for wellbeing checks or for correcting the setter's price anchor, and both gaps appear in calls that did not close.

marketing.who_buys: The sample is small: 14 sales calls, only 3 won in full and 5 more closed on a deposit or instalment, so treat these patterns as early signals, not rules. The people who paid were problem-aware, had the person paying on the call, and could say why now; the full wins (a hurt wife alone, a serial cheater, a couple stuck after the affair) all took a smaller first step (the first month or the $500 One Call Session) paid on the call rather than the full $4,500 or $5,400. Men who cheated and came alone all paid something but only in pieces, because money was tight or their wife held it. Non-buyers were mostly couples fresh from the discovery who heard the price before the pitch, compared providers, doubted 12 weeks could rebuild trust or found $1,800 a month too much on one income, plus a serial cheater who wanted to vet Barak first and a grieving woman who was not ready.
marketing.icp_gap: The closing doc pictures a couple or one partner ready to rebuild after infidelity who can invest low to mid four figures. Who actually shows up carries far more: past suicidal thoughts, choking and physical violence, bipolar and mania, cancer treatment, a son's recent death, and several on low or single incomes or paying in another currency, with threads showing people asking for licensed therapists and insurance cover. Who actually buys in full is narrower still: someone with their own money who accepts a one-month or one-session start on the call. Then you can decide whether that feels like the right solution for you. Fair?

examples.issue: Instead of the transition she announces she will 'go over' the investment first, and gives $5,400 before the pitch and before any temperature check.
examples.better: Well G. and S., based on everything you've told me, honestly, this is exactly the kind of situation Barak works with. So here's what I think makes the most sense. I can walk you through how Barak would approach getting you both from where things are now to staying together and going through with your wedding. Then you can decide whether that feels like the right solution for you. Fair?

coach_themes.label: Answers 'I need to think about it' with: thinking about it won't give the answers that talking to Barak will (script blank: from won calls)

examples.issue: A competing provider is the real objection and she answers with logistics (who they are meeting, when) instead of the think-about-it reframe.
examples.better: No problem at all. For a second, let's take the other meeting completely off the table. I just don't know that you thinking about it is necessarily going to give you the answers as much as talking to Barak will. Based purely on the process I just walked you through, do you feel like this is genuinely what you both need to get to staying together and going through with your wedding?

examples.issue: To 'give me some time to think about it' she offers to 'get creative with the plan', which treats an uncertainty objection as money.
examples.better: No problem at all. For a second, let's take money completely off the table. I just don't know that you thinking about it is necessarily going to give you the answers as much as talking to Barak will. What specifically are you unsure about?

coach_themes.label: Steps down to the first month (4 sessions) or a $500 One Call Session, credited toward the full program, only after the full pitch and only when the doubt is about certainty, not cash (script blank: from won calls)

examples.issue: Step-down to 'the first month ... around $1,500' with no statement that it counts toward the program, and CRM later records it as the whole contract.
examples.better: So the first month is the first four sessions, $1,500. If you decide to continue, that's already counted toward the full $4,500, so you're never paying twice.

examples.issue: Steps down to a $300 first call and a $100 'lowest that I have' deposit, neither in the sanctioned offer, and never says it counts toward the program.
examples.better: If you'd like to start smaller, the first month is four sessions for $1,500, or you can start with a One Call Session for $500 that's credited toward the full program if you continue.

coach_themes.label: Cheated-on branch: asks what goes through their head when the partner is out, and whether they are becoming a version of themselves they don't recognize

examples.issue: J. said she cannot always eat and wakes frightened every night and asked whether Barak deals with betrayal trauma or whether she needs to go elsewhere. Makena said Barak can help with that and went on, with no acknowledgement or referral.
examples.better: I'm so sorry, J.. Waking up frightened every night and struggling to eat is serious, and I don't want to skip past it. Barak's work is on the relationship and the choices behind what happened. It isn't treatment for trauma, so I'd encourage you to also see a therapist who specialises in betrayal trauma while you do this. Would you be open to that?

examples.issue: D. said "I can't live like that" and "If help can't help me, then at that point, then I have to choose the last option I have." Makena answered "Yeah." and went straight on to ask whether both were willing to try. It could mean leaving, but it could mean suicide, and she did not ask.
examples.better: D., I want to go back to something you said, that if help can't help you, you'd have to choose the last option you have. When you say that, do you mean leaving, or are you having thoughts of hurting yourself? I'm asking because it matters to me. If it's the second, please talk to your counselor today, or call or text 988.

coach_themes.label: Stops talking after the price

examples.issue: After "$5,400. If we have to break it down, we can" she kept talking about sessions and "that's the process" instead of stopping, and the "assuming we can figure out the financial side" question never came before the price discussion moved on.
examples.better: It's $5,400 for the full 12 weeks, or three payments of $1,800. Assuming we can figure out the financial side of things, is this something you both want to move forward with?

examples.issue: She says the price and keeps talking: in the same breath she offers the four-session start and financing, then agrees an improvised 2 x $750 split, so he never has to sit with the number or say whether it is a yes.
examples.better: So the 12-week program is $4,500, which you can split into three monthly payments of $1,500. Assuming we can figure out the financial side of things, is this something you want to move forward with?

coach_themes.label: Asks permission to be honest, names any mixed signals or justifications back to them, and says Barak can only help someone with a real will to change (added: not in script, from call evidence)

examples.issue: He says he choked his wife, went to jail, that she attempted suicide, and that he has no control over his emotions. She says 'I'm sorry to hear that', asks if he was physical with his kids, and moves on to the sale with a confident close.
examples.better: J., can I be honest with you? What you just told me about Melinda is serious, and before we talk about working with Barak I want to make sure you and Melinda are both safe right now. Is there anything going on at home that I should know about? And Barak can only help someone with a real will to change, so I want to hear from you what you will do differently.

coach_themes.label: If uncertain, says what matters is that it's the right fit and asks for a 1 to 10 ('this isn't what I need' to 'exactly the help I've been looking for')

examples.issue: When G. says only that it 'could be beneficial', she accepts it and never gets a number or finds what keeps him from a 9 or 10.
examples.better: Totally fair. And what matters most to me is that this is genuinely the right fit for you both. So if 1 is 'this isn't what I need at all' and 10 is 'this is exactly the kind of help I've been looking for', where are you right now? ... Gotcha. What's keeping you from being a 9 or 10?

coach_themes.label: Uses the 'over 80% of couples stay together' stat only as a track record, never as a promise for them (script blank: from won calls)

examples.issue: Uses the 80% couples stat as 'reassurance' for a single man, then says nothing should stop him from the same outcomes. That presents a track record as a promise.
examples.better: I'll be straight with you. Over 80% of the couples who come into Barak's program stay together, and that's a track record, not a promise for you. What I can promise is the process: by the end of the 12 weeks you'll know why you do this and whether you want a relationship, either way, and Barak will hold you accountable the whole way.

coach_themes.label: Asks what made them decide to get help now, and why not keep trying to figure it out themselves

examples.issue: Never asks why he is making this a priority now or what the pattern has cost him.
examples.better: What made you decide to actually get help with this now, instead of just continuing the way you have for the last six years? And can I ask you something more personal? What's all of this actually been costing you? Not financially, I mean you personally.

coach_themes.label: Digs into the why under the cheating: what feeling they were after or what need it filled, challenges the easy answer, and frames not knowing why as what the work with Barak is for (added: not in script, from call evidence)

examples.issue: L. is the one who cheated and is never asked why, or what the cheating gave him. C. volunteers the possible whys and the rep does not take them to him.
examples.better: L., when you look back at last September, what do you think you were looking for in that moment that you weren't getting? And if you don't know yet, that is exactly what the work with Barak is for.

coach_themes.label: Sends the agreement form for the plan they chose (script blank: from won calls)

examples.issue: Payment lands but no agreement form is sent and the first session is left for her to text back.
examples.better: Perfect, it went through. I'm sending you the agreement form for the first month and Barak's booking link now. You said 5 to 6 works. Let's pick your first session while we're on, for this week.

coach_themes.label: Asks: if nothing changes and in 6 months or a year it's the same fights, mistrust and resentment, 'what happens to the relationship?'

examples.issue: Never asks what happens if nothing changes, so the pitch and price land without a cost of inaction.
examples.better: Let me ask you this. If nothing actually changes from here, and six months or a year from now you're still holding it in and not able to be the husband M. needs, what happens to the relationship?

coach_themes.label: First objection, always pace: takes money off the table and asks if, based purely on the process, this is genuinely what they need to reach their desired outcome

examples.issue: On the first real objection after the price she went straight to the four-session step-down. The script says to pace first: take money off the table and test belief.
examples.better: Let's take the money off the table for a second. Based purely on the process we just went through, is this genuinely what you need to become the man you described, a man of integrity who can trust himself?

coach_themes.label: Cheated branch: asks the hardest part since, whether the partner can hear them or everything comes back to what they did, guilt, whether they understand why they cheated, and whether they have done everything to rebuild trust

examples.issue: N. said he pulled F. off the bed and "One time, I put my hands on her." Makena echoed one word ("Relationship?") and went on. No safety question, no check with F., no referral, and then she sold a couples program.
examples.better: N., I want to pause on what you just said about putting your hands on F.. F., I'd like to ask you directly: do you feel safe with N.? Barak works on trust and honesty. He doesn't work on safety from violence, so before we go any further I want to be sure you both have the right support for that. Is that something you're getting?

coach_themes.label: Stays on until the payment goes through, solving card, bank or link problems live (script blank: from won calls)

examples.issue: Left with the payment, the agreement form and the first booking all outstanding, with F. to pay "in about half an hour" from work.
examples.better: F., you've got a few minutes before work. Let's do the payment right now while I'm on the line, and as soon as it goes through I'll send the agreement form and Barak's booking link so we can pick your first session before you go.

exemplary.quote: M., how do you think that that would feel for you, knowing that?
exemplary.why: Asks the husband how it feels to hear his wife's answer about trusting herself.

exemplary.quote: Finances aside, like, do you believe, like, this will actually be helpful for you guys rebuilding trust and your happiness and the relationship?
exemplary.why: Paces the money objection and gets a clear yes before more price talk.

exemplary.quote: Today's Monday, do you want to set up a time on Wednesday, then, to reconnect?
exemplary.why: Dated reconnect instead of 'text me'.

exemplary.quote: And why are you looking to make this a priority now? Because it's been almost your whole life that you've been struggling with this.
exemplary.why: Asks why now and names the length of the problem in his own terms.

exemplary.quote: So I guess for you, are you willing to kind of put in the action that you need to become the better version of Paul? Are you actually willing to… to commit to that identity?
exemplary.why: Gets a spoken commitment tied to who he wants to become.

exemplary.quote: I can give you a text tonight in about an hour and a half or so, and if you're good to hop back on call, we can do that.
exemplary.why: A real time for the same evening instead of 'text me'.

exemplary.quote: was there any, like, emotional or, like, any sort of void that you can pinpoint of something that you were trying to fill?
exemplary.why: Goes under the cheating to the need it filled, which gives S. the 'low self-esteem' answer the pitch then uses.

exemplary.quote: you don't necessarily get the support you need to heal from this, and you're still having the same mistrust or resentment building 6 months from now, 12 months from now, what would happen to the relationship?
exemplary.why: Future-consequences question asked of both partners, each answers for themselves.

exemplary.quote: So, this program isn't about staying together at all costs, it's about discovering whether or not your relationship is worth saving.
exemplary.why: States the honest end state without a promise of staying together.

exemplary.quote: and if there's not a real will to change, he can't necessarily help you make any changes. Does that make sense?
exemplary.why: Honest mirror of his mixed signals, naming the condition for Barak helping.

exemplary.quote: I just don't know that, like, you thinking about it is necessarily gonna give you the answers as much as talking to him will.
exemplary.why: Answers think-about-it with the sanctioned reframe.

exemplary.quote: 500 just for… for one call. And then if you do end up deciding to continue, you can just use that towards the rest of the program
exemplary.why: Step-down after the full pitch, clearly credited to the program.

exemplary.quote: Um, C., how does that feel for you?
exemplary.why: Asks one partner how it feels to hear the other's answer to why he still wants the relationship.

exemplary.quote: Um, are you guys both open to doing, to starting with the four sessions
exemplary.why: Puts the start to both partners and gets a separate spoken yes from each.

exemplary.quote: Typically we do it all on the call.
exemplary.why: Holds the line when the prospect offers to pay later, and the payment lands on the call.

exemplary.quote: Would you wanna be with someone though that wouldn't want the best for you and for you to be happy and healthy?
exemplary.why: Works the real block, fear of her husband leaving, with a question before touching price.

exemplary.quote: Finances aside, though, is this something that you feel can actually help you gain the self-trust back, the emotional regulation, and find more peace?
exemplary.why: Paces the objection with money off the table.

exemplary.quote: Do you have access, like, to your bank account now, just so we can kind of square it away before I hop off the call with you?
exemplary.why: Stays on until payment is solved live.

exemplary.quote: In terms of the finances, is it kind of like, you have the investment, it's just a matter of being unsure about the program and the process? Is it… you have some of the finances, and we just need to find a way to break it down, or, like, none of the finances?
exemplary.why: Isolates money into have it, some of it, or none, and he confirms he is sure about the program.

exemplary.quote: Okay, yeah, are you able to do it now so we can get you booked in for the call?
exemplary.why: Stays on the call and works the payment live, including switching card to debit.

exemplary.quote: You'll meet with Barack next Monday, then.
exemplary.why: Leaves with a booked session inside the week.

exemplary.quote: Do you feel like you are ready to make the necessary changes to become the type of man that you actually want to be?
exemplary.why: Ties the commitment question to his own identity statement and gets a spoken yes.

exemplary.quote: Who do you feel like that will help allow you to become?
exemplary.why: Holds his own words (man of your word, integrity) and asks who he becomes; he answers "peaceful".

exemplary.quote: what is your fear of making that commitment?
exemplary.why: Works the real block with a question before touching price again.

exemplary.quote: Is it the case that you're… have the money, you're just uncertain about the program, some of the money, and we just kind of need to figure out a way to break it down? Or would this be, like, a complete stretch financially?
exemplary.why: Isolates the money into have it, some of it, or a real stretch, as the script wants.

exemplary.quote: Does that feel any different for you compared to when he says, but you said this, or but this happened?
exemplary.why: Asks the hurt partner how it lands when the other owns it, and surfaces the real accountability gap.

exemplary.quote: Can I ask you guys, like, what's stopping you from booking the first session with him, just to, like, see if he is a good fit?
exemplary.why: Asks about the real block before offering anything else.

exemplary.quote: do you want that for yourself, too, not just for her?
exemplary.why: Checks early that the cheating partner wants change for himself, before any pitch.

exemplary.quote: I guess, if nothing changes from here, or 6 months from now, you're still having kind of the same fights, same mistrust, resentment, like, what actually happens to the relationship?
exemplary.why: Script-true future-consequences question and she waited; D. answered "We're done."

exemplary.quote: You can be honest. No, nobody's forcing you to do it.
exemplary.why: Tests real intent when payment stalls instead of pushing the card harder.

exemplary.quote: And N., are you gonna be driving during this?
exemplary.why: Checks that N. is safe and present before starting.

exemplary.quote: when you say, like, a better person, what do you mean by that?
exemplary.why: Repeats his words and asks what he means, as the script wants.

exemplary.quote: Why do you have to? Because a lot of people don't.
exemplary.why: Gets him to say he is doing this for himself, in his own words.

exemplary.quote: Sorry to hear about your son, by the way.
exemplary.why: Acknowledges the loss briefly and lets her carry on.

exemplary.quote: say you worked with him for the next 3-6 months, like, what would be the ideal outcome for you?
exemplary.why: Flips her to the future in her own terms and gets "Get clarity".

exemplary.quote: what do you feel like will help give you certainty on the process?
exemplary.why: Asks what is unsure instead of reaching for a payment plan.

exemplary.quote: Do you believe that you can actively choose your wife while entertaining other people emotionally?
exemplary.why: Names his justification back to him without excusing it, which gets him to own it as emotional cheating.

exemplary.quote: Trust me, if you were not taking accountability for your part in this, we would absolutely be telling you because I know that that's what Barack is gonna do.
exemplary.why: Sets the accountability standard Barak will hold him to, in a warm tone.

exemplary.quote: Like say we get to the end of the 12 weeks with Barack, like what would be your ideal outcome?
exemplary.why: Future-paces to week 12 and lets him describe the outcome in his own words.

exemplary.quote: Before we kind of get into finances, is this something that you both feel can help you rebuild the trust and work through these issues?
exemplary.why: Takes money off the table and tests belief first, exactly as the script asks.

exemplary.quote: Are you guys able to resolve it all in one, or do you need to break it up a little bit?
exemplary.why: Isolates the money and moves the monthly plan to the one who needs it.

exemplary.quote: Do you know what kind of, like, feeling you're after when you are looking at
exemplary.why: Asks for the feeling under the cheating instead of accepting "it's my nature".
